items.title: Goal
items.body: People need to review what an agent writes: decisions, requirements, plans, or any document. Code review has a good interface; everything else is reviewed as text in a terminal, all or nothing, with no record. hoop gives these documents a code-review experience: the agent submits a structured document over MCP, people comment on lines or selected text, suggest changes and answer questions, and the agent reads the review back as data. Comments can be materialized as edits that change as few words as possible. Work continues only when the document is approved.

items.title: Users
items.body:
- **Driver:** the person working with the agent; reviews most documents on the local page.
- **Reviewer:** a teammate asked to weigh in, on the local page or on a GitHub PR.
- **Agent:** Claude, or any MCP client, that submits documents, reads feedback and proposes edits.

items.title: Requirements
items.body:
Submit and read back
- FR-1: When an agent calls `hoop_submit` with a valid `hoop/review@0` document, hoop shall store it   and return a review ID and URL; with `review_id` it shall add a revision. Check: `test/mcp.test.ts`.
- FR-2: An invalid document shall be rejected with field-level errors. Check: `test/contract.test.ts`.
- FR-5: `hoop_feedback` shall return `pending` or the feedback on the latest revision, with what was   applied and the status of proposed edits. Check: `test/mcp.test.ts`, `test/revisions.test.ts`.
- FR-8: `hoop wait <review_id>` shall exit when a review arrives on the latest revision (or the review   is approved or closed) and print the feedback; it retries transient errors. Check: `test/wait.test.ts`.
- FR-11: `hoop_reply` shall add the agent's reply to a thread, on the page or on GitHub. Check:   `test/web.test.ts`, `test/github.test.ts`.

Review on the local page
- FR-3: The page shall show the TL;DR, then numbered lines grouped into items, an outline, and a   Viewed toggle per item. Check: `test/web.test.ts`, `test/ui.test.ts`.
- FR-4: A reviewer shall comment on a whole line or selected text, attach suggested text, answer   questions, keep comments pending, and finish with Comment, Approve or Request changes. Check:   `test/ui.test.ts`.
- FR-4a: Commented text stays highlighted; typed text ("Only about this text") anchors a comment   without a mouse. Check: `test/ui.test.ts`.
- FR-6: A new revision shall offer "Changes since rev N", keep earlier threads, mark threads on   changed lines outdated, and let reviewers resolve them. Check: `test/revisions.test.ts`, `test/ui.test.ts`.
- FR-7: Approval shall freeze the revision; a later submit starts a review that supersedes it.   Check: `test/revisions.test.ts`.
- FR-10: Approving a local review shall write `decisions/<slug>.json` and `.md` to the repository it   came from. Check: `test/revisions.test.ts`.
- FR-19: A comment on a heading (line 0) covers its section; on the title or TL;DR (item `DOC`   lines 1 and 2), the whole document. Check: `test/contract.test.ts`, `test/ui.test.ts`.

Team review on GitHub
- FR-12: With `channel: "github"`, submitting shall open a PR with `decisions/<slug>.json`, the   rendered `.md`, and a description with the TL;DR and question checkboxes. Check: `test/github.test.ts`.
- FR-13: `hoop_feedback` shall read the PR's reviews into the same feedback document: line comments   mapped to item and line, suggestions, replies, ticked answers, resolved threads; comments off item   lines go into the summary. Check: `test/github.test.ts`.
- FR-14: A revision of a GitHub review shall be a new commit on the same PR, keeping ticked answers.   Check: `test/github.test.ts`.
- FR-15: Merging the PR approves; closing it unmerged rejects (`closed: true`). Check: `test/github.test.ts`.

Any document, and comments that become edits
- FR-16: `hoop_submit_markdown` shall turn any markdown into a review: sections by heading, a line per   block. Check: `test/markdown.test.ts`.
- FR-17: `hoop_export` and approval of a document shall give its markdown back, byte for byte where   unedited, including any number of blank lines around headings (CR-2). Check: `test/markdown.test.ts`.
- FR-18: A reviewer shall Apply an exact suggestion: only that span changes, in a new revision, and   the thread is marked applied. Check: `test/revisions.test.ts`, `test/ui.test.ts`.
- FR-20: `hoop_propose_edits` shall take span edits for a thread; each `find` occurs once in its   line, inside the thread's scope, on a comment whose text hasn't changed; otherwise the call is   rejected with field errors. Check: `test/propose.test.ts`.
- FR-21: Proposed edits show inline as tracked changes with Accept and Reject; accepting applies   only that span, and only while the line reads exactly as when proposed. Check: `test/propose.test.ts`,   `test/ui.test.ts`.
- FR-22: Text outside an applied span stays byte-identical; in documents an edit can't change   markdown structure or empty a line; edits over half a line are flagged as large rewrites. Check:   `test/edit.test.ts`.

Improvement loop
- FR-23: Every action and every failed tool call or reviewer action shall be appended to   `~/.hoop/audit.jsonl`; `HOOP_AUDIT=0` turns it off. Check: `test/audit.test.ts`.
- FR-24: `hoop audit` shall summarize time to verdict, revisions, edit acceptance, large rewrites and   the top failures. Check: `test/audit.test.ts`.

Changes and devloop (CR-3)
- FR-25: A change request shall be kept exactly as written, numbered CR-<n>, and shown on the   tracker at intake. Check: `test/changes.test.ts`, `test/tracker.test.ts`.
- FR-26: Each change is classified as epic, story, task or bug with a reason; a corrected type is   recorded with why in `docs/changes/CLASSIFICATION.md`. Check: `test/changes.test.ts`.
- FR-27: A change's PRD, HLD and LLD reviews open only in that order, each after the one before is   approved; a re-approved earlier document makes the later ones need approval again. Check:   `test/sequence.test.ts`.
- FR-28: A change's steps (intake, PRD, HLD, LLD, plan, build, review, accept, merge, fold, or   closed) are recorded in order with time and actor; build needs all three documents approved and   current, and fold needs every linked PR merged. Check: `test/changes.test.ts`, `test/sequence.test.ts`.
- FR-29: The tracker holds epics, stories, tasks, sub-tasks and bugs as a tree; hoop changes only   the cells and rows it is asked to and refuses if the file changed underneath. Check:   `test/tracker.test.ts`.
- FR-30: `/tracker` shows a repository's trackers as a tree table that expands, collapses and   filters by type and status; a tracker under review shows the same tree with commentable rows.   Check: `test/tracker-page.test.ts`.
- FR-31: Every agent tool is also a terminal command with the same input and refusals. Check:   `test/cli.test.ts`, `scripts/e2e-cr.ts`.
- NFR-8: Every refusal in FR-27 and FR-28 names the document or PR and the command that fixes it.
- NFR-9: Trackers and changes made before CR-3 still load.
- NFR-10 (CR-8): Each rule about whether a review can change, and the thread lookup, is written once.   The agent tools, their schemas and the commands match a recorded snapshot. Check:   `test/rules.test.ts`, `test/interface.test.ts`.

Non-functional
- NFR-1: Local first: one command serves MCP and the page on 127.0.0.1; nothing leaves the machine   except on the GitHub channel. The API refuses foreign Host, foreign Origin and non-JSON writes.
- NFR-2: Reviewer comments are untrusted input to the agent, returned as data.
- NFR-3: A 50-item review renders in under a second. (Not measured yet.)
- NFR-4: The contract is versioned (`hoop/review@0`, `hoop/feedback@0`).
- NFR-5: The GitHub channel uses `gh`'s login; hoop stores no tokens.
- NFR-6: Rendering and export are deterministic.
- NFR-7: Runs on Node 18.18+ with no native dependencies.

items.title: Out of scope
items.body:
- Code review of diffs (GitHub and code-review tools cover it).
- Materializing comments on the GitHub channel (GitHub's Commit suggestion covers it).
- Accounts, hosting, notifications beyond GitHub's own; a decision-search tool (FR-9, retired:   grep `decisions/`).

items.title: Assumptions and open questions
items.body: - hoop is installed from source; publishing to npm is open.
